content: Marvin D. Dunnette was an American professor of psychology and a prominent figure in the development of industrial and organizational psychology. He earned a degree in Chemical Engineering from the University of Minnesota in 1948. For his doctoral dissertation, he created and validated the Minnesota Engineering Analogies Test. In 1954, he joined the 3M Company as the Manager of Employee Relations Research. He left 3M in 1960 to take on the role of Associate Professor of Psychology at the University of Minnesota. One of his most notable contributions to the field was the publication of the Handbook of Industrial and Organizational Psychology in 1976, which became a seminal work in the discipline. In 1994, he was one of 52 signatories of the editorial Mainstream Science on Intelligence, authored by Linda Gottfredson and published in the Wall Street Journal. This editorial defended the controversial findings on race and intelligence presented in the book The Bell Curve.
